issues.legal_issue: A legislature may levy a tax only under a specific taxing entry, and cannot derive taxing power from a general entry concerning the subject matter.
material_facts: The State argued that its power to legislate concerning intoxicating liquors also authorized it to levy a cess on them.
The levy was challenged as a tax on excise-related receipts.
issues.conclusion: The power to legislate concerning intoxicating liquors did not itself authorize a tax; taxing power had to come from a specific taxing entry. The power under the relevant entry for alcoholic liquors was limited to excise duty on manufacture or production.
issues.legal_principle: Legislative power may include incidental and subsidiary powers, but the power to tax is not incidental or subsidiary to power over a general subject. A tax requires a specific taxing entry. The Court relied on M.P.V. Sundararamier & Co. v. State of Andhra Pradesh and R.C. Jall v. Union of India, and considered List II Entries 8 and 51 of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.

predicates.challenge_to_state_tax_levy: A party challenged a tax levied by a state.
predicates.state_relies_on_general_subject_entry: The state relied on an entry concerning a general subject, rather than a specific taxing entry, as authority for the tax.

issues.definition: When a state tax is challenged and the state relies on a general subject entry, the rule requires the taxing power to come from a specific taxing entry.

issues.legal_issue: A payment for the privilege of retail sale, unrelated to manufacture or production, is not excise revenue on which a cess limited to excise revenue can be imposed.
material_facts: The consideration paid for the exclusive privilege of retail vending was collected through auction and called shop-rent.
The payment represented the value of the right to sell and had no relation to the production or manufacture of the liquor.
The education cess was imposed on specified categories of revenue, including excise revenue.
issues.conclusion: Shop-rent was not excise revenue within the meaning of the applicable schedule, so education cess could not be levied on it.
issues.legal_principle: Under List II Entry 51, excise duty on alcoholic liquor is tied to manufacture or production. A payment for the privilege of selling an excisable article is not excise duty merely because it concerns that article; clear charging language is required to make it a duty of excise. The Court followed M/s. Guruswamy & Company v. State of Mysore and relied on the principles in R.C. Jall v. Union of India.

predicates.challenge_to_cess_levy: A party challenged a cess imposed on a payment connected with the sale of goods.
predicates.cess_base_limited_to_revenue_categories: The governing levy applies only to specified categories of revenue.
predicates.shop_payment_for_sale_privilege_not_prod: A seller paid the state for an exclusive retail-sale privilege, and the payment was unrelated to producing or manufacturing the goods.

issues.definition: Where a challenged cess is limited to specified revenue categories and the payment is for a retail-sale privilege rather than production, the rule is that the cess does not apply to that payment.

issues.legal_issue: Tree-related charges that have ceased to be levied separately and have merged into a sale-privilege payment cannot be enforced as separate charges where the relevant cess was not lawfully levied.
material_facts: Tree-tax and tree-rent were originally charged separately but a notification discontinued their separate levy and merged them into shop-rent.
A fixed portion of the relevant collections was treated as local cess and diverted to local bodies.
The education cess on tree-tax and tree-rent had not been lawfully levied under the relevant arrangement.
issues.conclusion: The State could not enforce liability to pay tree-tax or tree-rent against the contractors.
issues.legal_principle: Where charges have ceased to be levied separately and have merged into another payment, and the claimed cess on them was not lawfully levied, liability to pay those charges cannot be enforced. The Court considered the schedule to the Mysore Elementary Education Act, 1941, as amended, and Article 265 of the Constitution.

rule.if: challenge_to_cess_collection and separate_tree_charges_discontinued and tree_charges_merged_into_sale_payment and no_lawful_cess_previously_collected

predicates.challenge_to_cess_collection: A party challenged the state's collection of a cess or related charges.
predicates.separate_tree_charges_discontinued: The state stopped levying tree-related charges separately.
predicates.tree_charges_merged_into_sale_payment: The former tree-related charges were incorporated into a payment for a sale privilege.
predicates.no_lawful_cess_previously_collected: The relevant cess had not been lawfully levied before the claimed liability was enforced.

issues.definition: If separate tree charges were discontinued and merged into a sale payment, and the relevant cess had not been lawfully collected, the rule is that the state cannot enforce liability for those charges.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a cess on shop-rent could be supported as a tax on luxuries need not be decided when the governing levy does not impose an independent cess and shop-rent is outside its specified revenue base.
material_facts: The education cess was imposed as a cess on specified categories of land, forest, and excise revenue, not as an independent cess.
Shop-rent was not land revenue, forest revenue, or excise revenue.
The State argued that the cess could alternatively be supported as a tax on luxuries.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not determine whether the State could levy a tax on luxuries under the relevant constitutional entry, because shop-rent was outside the statutory base of the education cess.
issues.legal_principle: A levy must be imposed by the governing statute and within its stated base. The Court considered List II Entry 62 of the Seventh Schedule and the schedule to the Mysore Elementary Education Act, 1941, as amended, but held that the Entry 62 question did not arise on these facts.

rule.if: challenge_to_cess_levy and cess_not_independent_of_specified_revenue_base and payment_outside_specified_revenue_base and state_invokes_luxury_tax_entry

predicates.challenge_to_cess_levy: A party challenged a cess imposed on a payment.
predicates.cess_not_independent_of_specified_revenu: The cess is imposed only on specified categories of revenue and is not an independent levy.
predicates.payment_outside_specified_revenue_base: The payment on which the cess is claimed does not fall within the specified revenue categories.
predicates.state_invokes_luxury_tax_entry: The state argues that the levy can be supported as a tax on a luxury.

issues.definition: When a challenged cess depends on a specified revenue base, the payment falls outside that base, and the state invokes a luxury-tax power, the rule is that the question of that power is not reached.

issues.legal_issue: An auction condition agreeing to pay a cess cannot create statutory liability when the governing law does not impose the cess.
material_facts: The auction conditions required contractors to pay education cess.
The governing statute did not impose the education cess on shop-rent.
The State relied on the contractors' agreement as an alternative basis for payment.
issues.conclusion: A contractual auction condition could not create liability to pay the cess in the absence of a statutory levy.
issues.legal_principle: Liability to pay a cess is statutory; if the statute does not effectuate the levy, liability does not arise merely from an auction condition. The Court applied Article 265 of the Constitution and the statutory scheme of the Mysore Elementary Education Act, 1941, as amended.

predicates.challenge_to_cess_liability: A party disputes liability to pay a cess.
predicates.auction_terms_require_cess_payment: The terms for an auction or licence state that the participant must pay a cess.
predicates.statute_does_not_impose_cess_on_payment: The governing law does not impose the cess on the payment in question.

issues.definition: When auction terms require a cess but the governing law does not impose it on the payment, the rule is that the auction condition cannot create liability.
